First, let's sketch our region $D:$ 

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14111253/assets/eb8745d968da24a8500bd079638b17bc461ab2d97b93d1d1a7d6d4834365bb5a.png)

Notice that 

$$
\text{Area}(D)=\frac{1}{4}\cdot \pi \cdot {1}^{2}=\frac{\pi }{4}.
$$

The average value of the function over a region $D$ is given by

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{1}{\text{Area}(D)}\,{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\,\text{d}A.
$$

We will use the change of variables formula in the form

$$
{∬}_{D}f(x,y)\text{ }dA={∬}_{Δ}\text{ }f(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\text{ }drd\theta .
$$

In polar coordinates $(r,\theta ),$ the region can be expressed as 

$$
Δ={(r,\theta )\,:\,0\le r\le 1,\,0\le \theta \le \frac{\pi }{2}}.
$$

Using the change of variables formula, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{D}4xy\,dA & ={∬}_{Δ}4(r\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )(r\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )\,r\,\text{d}r\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}{\int }_{0}^{1}4{r}^{3}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta {\int }_{0}^{1}4{r}^{3}\,\text{d}r\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,{[{r}^{4}]}_{0}^{1}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta (1-0)\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{0}^{\pi /2}\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta \operatorname{sin}⁡\theta \,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =\frac{1}{2}[{sin}^{2}⁡\theta ]_{0}^{\pi /2} \\  & =\frac{1}{2}({sin}^{2}⁡(\frac{\pi }{2})-{sin}^{2}⁡(0)) \\  & =\frac{1}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 

$$
{f}_{\text{ave}}=\frac{4}{\pi }\cdot \frac{1}{2}=\frac{2}{\pi }.
$$
